summary: untested cell: capped-delta-accept × owner-answer-while-check-pending → owner's answer settles the gate, the pending delta check's reservation is released and a later `check` is refused. answerGate never touches state.carry or the carry-check reservation, so after an approve the reserved estimate stays in spend.json and state.carry still reads check_pending; no test exercises this path.
fix: Have answerGate close a pending carry check (release the reservation, mark state.carry superseded) and add a test that answers the gate directly while CARRY_CHECK is pending.

summary: While a delta check is pending (state.carry.verdict=check_pending), the run stays status=gate_pending. So next and submit print CARRY_CHECK: and then the full GATE:/GATE_SPEND:/RELAY: block from gateLines (lines 202 and 240). The revise path does the same: approveOrRegate (lib/autoplan-revise.ts:115) falls through to 'GATE: ... needs the owner'. On Capy, the RELAY line tells the lane to send the owner brief to its Captain, and the brief has no check_pending state: it renders a normal pending gate with a reply invitation. A driver that follows DRIVER steps 3 and 7 together asks the owner and dispatches the carry reviewer at the same time. That defeats the no-second-ask goal. It is also the trigger for the specialist's answer-while-pending cell: if the check passes first, the owner's later reply hits PHASE_NOT_AWAITING on a run that is already complete.
fix: When state.carry is check_pending for the current gate_rev, suppress gateLines/RELAY (and the approveOrRegate GATE line) and print only CARRY_CHECK/NEXT. Alternatively, have the captain brief render 'delta check pending, do not relay' for that state.

summary: isDoIt is meant to accept only the owner's own 'do it' and to reject a Captain's relay of one. The only exclusion is a prefix that starts with the literal word 'captain'. Checked with node: 'GStack Minder: do it', 'the captain: do it' and 'agent: do it' all match. owner_reply is free text supplied by the relaying agent through --owner-reply, so a relay labeled with the Captain's name (or any other label) lets the carry take new auto items under 'do it' that the owner never saw. The record and the brief then state that these items were taken under the owner's words.
fix: Accept only a bare 'do it' (with optional punctuation), or require that a prefix name match the configured owner (for example the --by owner name). Do not blacklist one word.

summary: Once gate.json carries eli5, the brief reads the four sections and the ELI5 from that snapshot, which finishGate takes when the gate is written, and no longer from the reviewed plan. Two problems follow. First, every new gate now gets eli5 regardless of when the run started, so an in-flight run whose plan predates ## ELI5 turns CAPTAIN_BRIEF_INCOMPLETE at its next gate. The troubleshooting note ('older runs render as before') is wrong for these runs. Second, the documented fix (add the section, revise, render again) no longer clears the error at gate_pending: a quiet revise that reopens nothing updates the active plan but does not rewrite gate.json, so the stale empty eli5.summary keeps the brief 'Not ready for approval'.
fix: Fall back to the live reviewed plan when it is newer than the gate.json snapshot (compare plan_file_sha256), or refresh gate.json eli5 on revise. Require ELI5 only for runs initialized by the new version.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE, High] A pending delta check can overwrite a newer owner answer at the same gate (lib/autoplan-carry.ts:177, then carry() -> answerGate). The guard in submitCarryCheck checks only `carry.verdict === 'check_pending' && status === 'gate_pending' && carry.gate_rev === state.gate_rev`. It never checks that p1 at that gate is still unanswered. The finishGate output prints both the gate render and the CARRY_CHECK line, so the relaying agent can show the gate to the owner while it dispatches the check. If the owner answers p1c (interrogate), the gate stays gate_pending at the same gate_rev and the guard still passes. A later `gstack-autoplan check` then calls answerGate with `p1<recommended>` built from the gate N words, which silently replaces the owner's newer "interrogate" with an approval. If the owner also chose item overrides along with p1c, the carry reply sends the recommended options instead, so it either overwrites those choices or makes answerGate throw (see finding 2). Fix: refuse the check (and release its reservation) when any decision row at c.gate_rev is no longer pending. Also have answerGate clear `state.carry` when a non-carry answer arrives.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE, Medium] submitCarryCheck is not transactional, and a failure after the bind cannot be retried (lib/autoplan-carry.ts:196-218). These steps happen in order before writeState: gate.json is rewritten with carry_check and `flags.push(...)`, carry-check-g<rev>.bound.md is written with mode 0o444 (line 200), and the ledger is settled (line 201). Then assess() and carry() -> answerGate run with no try/catch. If either throws (GATE_REPLY_UNPARSED from the finding 1 path, a journal read error, or appendTrailRow failing), state.json still says check_pending. A retry then fails with EACCES on the existing read-only bound file (for any non-root user), and on the blocking path it pushes the carry-check flag onto the gate items a second time. The only way out is `--unavailable`, which discards a check that was valid. Fix: validate and compute everything first, write the bound file last (or accept an existing file with identical bytes), and wrap the carry in the same refuse-on-error handling evaluateCarry uses.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE, Medium] The delta-check reservation leaks whenever the check is not bound through `check` (lib/autoplan-carry.ts:139; lib/autoplan-gate.ts answerGate). dispatchCheck reserves `${run}-c${rev}` in the spend ledger. Only submitCarryCheck releases or settles it. If the owner answers the gate directly (the documented fallback is "relay the gate as today"), or a later gate_rev supersedes the check, the reservation stays in worst_case_usd for the rest of the run. With --spend-cap set, every leaked check (default estimate up to the $5 per-gate cap) shrinks the budget for later rounds and can trip SPEND_CAP refusals on legitimate reviews. The error path has the same leak: if fs.writeFileSync(prompt) at line 142 throws after the reservation, evaluateCarry's catch (line 121) refuses but never releases. Fix: release any outstanding carry check in answerGate and finishGate, and in the catch after a reservation.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE, Medium] A failure to write the trail can leave the run stuck after gate.json moves (lib/autoplan-carry.ts:71 record(), lines 121-122). record() calls appendTrailRow on <out>/decisions.tsv. If that write throws (a read-only file, a full disk, a flaky drive mount), the catch in evaluateCarry calls refuse() -> record() -> appendTrailRow again, which throws out of finishGate. By then gate.json and decisions.jsonl are already at rev N+1 and state.gate_rev has been bumped in memory, but writeState never runs. On disk, gate.json says N+1 and state.json says N, and each resume calls finishGate again and fails the same way. Run artifacts now depend on a best-effort audit trail. Fix: make the trail append best-effort (catch and journal the failure) inside record().

A truncated or corrupt archive (for example from an interrupted reopen) throws before anything is written, so the run cannot reach a gate even with --no-carry-forward. summary: [FIXABLE, Low] The "do it" detector accepts relayed agent prefixes (lib/autoplan-carry.ts:37). The `(?!captain\b)` lookahead only excludes text that starts with the word "captain". label: INVESTIGATE
summary: [INVESTIGATE, Medium] The carry check is self-attested, and its gates can be bypassed by the agent that benefits from the carry (lib/autoplan-carry.ts:192-199). The family check trusts the `--model` string the caller supplies. `--same-family "<any text>"` turns off both the same-family and the unknown-family refusals. The result file's only binding is the delta SHA, and that SHA is printed in the prompt the same agent holds. So the agent driving the run can write a "No findings." result and turn the owner's earlier approval into an approval of an unreviewed post-cap edit. The phase submit path has the same trust model, but here the output is an owner approval recorded on their behalf (and imported into the approvals record), so the stakes are higher. Deciding whether a carry needs a stronger witness, or whether `--same-family` should force the gate to the owner, needs a human.

summary: [INVESTIGATE, Low] The plan-unchanged check accepts any change made through `revise`, at any time (lib/autoplan-carry.ts assess(): it sets `expected` from the last plan_revised after gate_written for gate N). label: INVESTIGATE
summary: [INVESTIGATE, Low] Runner rows can be attributed to the wrong run in the decision trail (lib/autoplan-carry.ts:71). The runner appends rows to <out>/decisions.tsv with no start row of its own. CREW rule 27 allows lanes to keep their trail at `<run dir>/decisions.tsv`. Runner rows written after a lane's start row fall inside that lane's stretch, so the lane's pre-READY audit sees rows it never wrote. A carry or refusal row is also written for every gate_rev >= 2, which adds noise.

label: High
summary: **High — A revision can expand the approved plan and inherit the old approval without an authorization check.** `lib/autoplan-carry.ts:93–110` `assess()` replaces the approved source hash with the hash of every subsequent `plan_revised` event. It then checks only that the current source matches that latest revision and that no new gate item requires an answer. It never establishes that the revision contains only the changes the owner accepted. For example, after the owner accepts a retry flag, the relayer can incorporate that flag and add a new recurring service or paid integration in the same revision. If the normal review rounds produce no user-challenge items, gate 2 is automatically approved under the owner's gate-1 words, even when those words were merely `rec`. Normal reviewers assess the revised plan, not whether each change was authorized; only the capped-delta prompt explicitly checks authorization. The new default therefore converts a reviewer's silence into owner approval for scope or cost the owner never saw. Require a delta-to-accepted-changes check on changed plans before carrying, not only when a phase hit its round cap.

label: High
summary: **High — A failed delta check is omitted from the Captain's owner-facing approval brief.** `lib/autoplan-carry.ts:204–211`, `lib/captain-brief.ts:110–129` When the delta reviewer finds a High/Critical problem, `submitCarryCheck()` stores its title only in the delta item's `flags` and stores a severity/count summary in `gate.carry_check`. It does not add that finding to `findings.jsonl` or the build tasks, and it leaves the delta's recommendation as “accept the unreviewed delta.” The prescribed Capy relay is `gstack-owner-brief render --captain`, but that renderer prints neither item flags nor `carry_check`; it still recommends `rec` and accepting the delta. Thus a reviewer can explicitly detect an unauthorized scope change or a data-loss defect, yet the person deciding gets a brief that hides the detected problem and recommends approval. If they follow that recommendation, the problem is also absent from the generated remediation tasks. Render the failed check and its findings prominently in the Captain brief, and preserve them in the findings/task artifacts before soliciting approval.

label: Medium
summary: **Medium — Failed or unavailable checks leave stale artifact hashes, making their checkpoints unrestorable.** `lib/autoplan-carry.ts:185–189,206–221` Both the unavailable and failed-result paths rewrite `gate.json`, then call only `writeState(state)`. Its `artifacts['gate.json'].sha256` still describes the file exported by `finishGate()`. `validateRun()` checks that hash (`lib/headless-artifacts.ts:457–466`), and `restoreCheckpoint()` requires the staged run to pass validation (`lib/autoplan-checkpoint.ts`), so a checkpoint published immediately after either successful `check` command fails restoration with `ARTIFACT_STALE`. This is precisely the path where the workflow pauses for the owner and needs durable recovery. Refresh the artifact manifest before writing state and publishing the checkpoint. The passing-check path has a related stale hash: `carry()` adds `carry_check`/`carried_under` marks to `decisions.jsonl` after `answerGate()` already exported its hash (`lib/autoplan-carry.ts:162–164`), so it also needs a final export before checkpointing.

summary: dispatchCheck reserves the carry-check attempt in spend.json, and only `check` ever releases or settles it. While the check is pending, `next`, `submit` and `close` also print the GATE: and relay lines (bin/gstack-autoplan:202 and 240), so the relayer can send the gate to the owner. If the owner answers it, or a revise moves gate_rev, the reservation is never released. It is not journaled as dispatched, so releaseUndispatched only clears it on a deferred close. Until then it inflates worst_case and GATE_SPEND, and it can SPEND_CAP-refuse later reruns.

summary: The bound carry-check copy is written in place with mode 0444, unlike submit's tmp-plus-rename seal. A retried `check` then fails EACCES on the read-only file, so only --unavailable can recover.

label: FIXABLE
summary: Owner relay races the delta check; a carry can silently overrule an owner reply already in flight. Where: lib/autoplan-carry.ts dispatchCheck (126-155) leaves status=gate_pending; bin/gstack-autoplan gateLines (210-214) is still printed by next/close/submit/check whenever status is gate_pending, and it carries the capyRelayLine RELAY instruction. The owner brief rendered at that moment shows p1 pending with "Reply rec". Failure: the driver is told in the same output to RELAY the gate to the owner and to dispatch the CARRY_CHECK reviewer. If it does both and the check passes first, carry() (line 162) answers the gate with the owner's old words and the run goes to complete. The owner's later reply (possibly "p1e" reject or an override) then hits answerGate's PHASE_NOT_AWAITING guard (autoplan-gate.ts 386) and is not recorded anywhere, while the approval record says the owner's words carried. If the owner answers first, the agent's check fails with PHASE_NOT_AWAITING (finding 2 covers the leak that leaves behind). Fix: while state.carry.verdict === 'check_pending' for the current gate_rev, print the CARRY_CHECK/NEXT lines instead of GATE/RELAY (or print a "do not relay until check" line), and have the captain brief say "carry check pending" instead of inviting a reply.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The carry-check spend reservation leaks when anything other than gstack-autoplan check moves the gate. Where: lib/autoplan-carry.ts 139 reserves `<run>-c<rev>` in spend.json; only submitCarryCheck releases (185) or settles it. answerGate, revise, and reopen paths never touch it, and releaseUndispatched (autoplan-budget.ts 147) runs only on deferred closes. Failure: the owner answering directly (the natural result of finding 1), a revise that writes a newer gate, or a driver that never runs check leaves the reservation in ledger.reserved. summarize().worst_case_usd then includes it, so a reopened phase's admission check in nextStep (`before.worst_case_usd + fresh.length * estimate.usd > spend_cap_usd`) and later reserve() calls can stop the run with a spurious spend-cap refusal, and GATE_SPEND overstates spend. Fix: release the carry-check reservation when answerGate accepts an answer for that gate_rev or when finishGate writes a newer gate while state.carry is check_pending.

label: FIXABLE
summary: finishGate can now crash on a corrupt or partial gate archive, before the evaluateCarry try/catch protects anything. Where: lib/autoplan-gate.ts previousGate (291-302) does an unguarded JSON.parse of gate.json and every gate.r<rev>[.v<k>].json, and is called at 312 outside evaluateCarry's try. gateEvidence's copyFileSync (inside the journal call at 333) is also outside it. Failure: finishGate used to just overwrite gate.json. Now a truncated gate.json (a flaky Drive mount or a checkpoint restore, both conditions the code already plans for) throws out of finishGate on next/close/submit/resume/revise, and the run can never write its next gate. Carry-forward is optional, but this path makes it a hard dependency of gate writing. Fix: wrap previousGate and gateEvidence in the same fail-to-refuse handling (return undefined / refuse with a reason) so carry problems can only cost the carry, never the gate.

summary: Carry bookkeeping failures leave state that contradicts itself. Where: lib/autoplan-carry.ts record (67-73) writes the journal, then decisions.tsv through appendTrailRow, with no guard. evaluateCarry's catch (121) calls refuse → record again. Failure: (a) if appendTrailRow throws (EACCES, ENOSPC, or a Drive mount hiccup), the catch's refuse() throws the same way and escapes finishGate after gate.json, decisions.jsonl and the gate_written journal row exist but before the caller's writeState, which leaves a half-written gate. (b) In carry(), answerGate (162) has already approved the run and called closeDraftDirections, rewriting active_plan, before record() runs. If record then throws, the catch records verdict=refused and prints "CARRY: no" while state.status is complete with carried answers in decisions.jsonl. Fix: make the trail append best-effort (catch and journal the failure), and do not run refuse() after answerGate has applied.

label: FIXABLE
summary: submitCarryCheck is not atomic, and its 0444 bound file blocks a retry. Where: lib/autoplan-carry.ts 186-226. gate.json is rewritten, carry-check-g<rev>.bound.md is written mode 0o444 (200), and spend is settled, all before carry()/answerGate and the final writeState. Failure: any throw after line 200 (answerGate validation, journal I/O) leaves state.carry at check_pending with gate.json and spend.json already mutated. The obvious retry then fails with EACCES on writeFileSync to the read-only bound file (non-root), so the only way out is --unavailable, which discards a passing check and sends the gate to the owner. Fix: write the bound file last, through a temp file plus rename (or unlink first), and write gate.json/spend only after the verdict is applied.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: The "another model family" guarantee depends on what the driver says about itself and is only partly enforced. Where: lib/autoplan-carry.ts 192-195. --model is a free string the driver supplies, and the family is compared only with state.native_model. When native_model is unset, any recognized family passes, including the <reader>'s (a plan reviewer). --same-family "<any text>" bypasses the check entirely, and family=unknown is also accepted with it. Risk: the delta check is the only review an unreviewed post-cap plan edit gets before the owner's approval is reused. A driver (or a confused agent) can bind a same-family or self-written result and carry. Decide whether to also compare against the outside model, refuse when native_model is unknown, and record --same-family as a flag on the approval row.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: "do it" carries unseen items with no severity bound, and its Captain-relay exclusion is a prefix heuristic. Where: lib/autoplan-carry.ts 37 (DO_IT) and assess's do-it branch. Any kind:auto, no-cap item whose changes is not scope/cost/direction is taken, and that includes High/Critical re-review findings (auto items are built from findings at autoplan-gate.ts 226/235), plus items whose recommended option has changes_plan (which can push the run into amend_pending while the carry reason says "plan unchanged since the accepted changes"). The regex rejects only a prefix starting with the word "captain". "Minder captain: do it", "relay: do it" or "GStack Minder: do it" all count as the owner's words. Risk: owner authority gets applied to decisions the owner never saw on the strength of a relayed string. Consider excluding High+ findings and changes_plan options from do-it, and recording the relay provenance instead of parsing it out of the words.

label: FIXABLE
summary: import --stack is "every branch, or none" only for branch existence, not for writes. Where: bin/gstack-approvals importStack (69-96). The loop writes branch by branch. A locate()/importAutoplan() error returns early at 81/83 after earlier branches were written, and appendRows errors are collected while the loop continues. Failure: the docs (capy/skill/gstack/captain.md "every branch, or none", the HELP text) promise atomicity, but a mid-loop failure leaves some stack PRs with the approval row and others without. A controller checking a single PR's row before training could pass one PR of a half-recorded stack. Imports are idempotent, so retrying is safe, but nothing tells the caller which branches still need it in the early-return paths. Fix: resolve every locate()/importAutoplan() before the first append, and reword the docs to "checked first; a write failure names the branches left".

label: FIXABLE
summary: The ELI5 requirement hits in-flight runs that the docs say are exempt. Where: lib/autoplan-gate.ts 241-242 always adds eli5 to every new gate; lib/captain-brief.ts 86 marks ELI5 missing whenever gate.eli5 exists with an empty summary. Failure: docs/troubleshooting.md says "older runs render as before", but a run started before this release that writes its next gate under the new code (a regate after revise, or a reopen) now gets "Not ready for approval" / CAPTAIN_BRIEF_INCOMPLETE until its plan grows a ## ELI5. Adding that section changes the plan file's bytes, which also defeats carry-forward for that gate. Fix: write eli5 only for runs whose gstack_version is at least the release that added it (or skip the ELI5 requirement when the plan never had one at init), or correct the docs.

label: FIXABLE
summary: The delta check binds the prompt's sha, but nothing re-checks the plan when the result is submitted. Where: lib/autoplan-carry.ts 197 checks the result receipt against check.delta_sha256, and 213 re-runs assess, which verifies the plan file sha and PLAN_SOURCE_CHANGED but never recomputes the active_plan vs plan-at-gate.r<m> diff. Risk: an active_plan edit that does not trip driftLine between dispatch and check would carry over a delta the reviewer never read. This is narrow, but cheap to close: recompute the diff sha at check time and refuse on mismatch.

Where: lib/autoplan-revise.ts 206 re-reads `file` at commit time instead of hashing the bytes revise staged earlier (163-164). If the file changes in between, the journal records the newer bytes as the reviewed revision, and assess (expected sha) will accept that newer file. Hash the staged text instead.

label: FIXABLE
summary: Usability and output defects. - bin/gstack-autoplan doCheck's usage, the DRIVER text and the NEXT line present `--unavailable "<reason>"` as standalone, but submitCarryCheck (179) requires --attempt first, so `check --out d --unavailable x` fails with ATTEMPT_MISMATCH. - In reviseRun (213-218), a carry that approves inside approveOrRegate is followed by a second closeDraftDirections and a second `APPROVED:` line. Output parsers then see the APPROVED line twice. - lib/autoplan-run.ts reviewEstimateLine prints "rounds uncapped" for interactive runs (max_rounds null), which is accurate, but it gives docs-only CEO one voice by assumption. label: High
summary: A clean carry-check result can be replayed against a different plan. `lib/autoplan-carry.ts:133-147,196-199` hashes only the added and removed lines, dropping all unchanged context and line positions. The receipt does not bind the complete current plan, the accepted amendments, or the attempt. For example, changing `allow = false` to `allow = true` under `# Trusted administrator` and making the same change under `# Unauthenticated visitor` produce identical receipts, despite materially different security consequences. I exercised the actual `lineDiff` and `parseReviewResult` functions: both changes produced `0dd084c0c9286891ce9e1ea846b9aaeb2326fe06e57124f196fb3d9e9ca0f161`, and an empty-findings result for the first passed validation for the second. `check --attempt <current> --result <old-result>` accepts an arbitrary result path, so a stale or deliberately reused clean review can automatically approve an unreviewed security-sensitive plan. Bind the receipt to the full review input, including the before/after plans, accepted changes, and attempt identity.

label: High
summary: A partially answered gate is treated as an approved source gate. `lib/autoplan-carry.ts:84-92` checks only the earlier P1 decision, not whether the earlier gate's other required approvals were answered or whether its answer reached the full-answer path. This is not equivalent: with a required `uc1` scope decision, `parseReply("p1b", ...)` and `applyReply(...)` leave `uc1` pending while marking P1 approved. `answerGate` explicitly returns `GATE_PENDING` before creating amendments or journaling a completed answer in this case (`lib/autoplan-gate.ts:409-416`). `revise` nevertheless accepts a gated run. If the revised review no longer emits that scope challenge, the next gate can contain only P1; `assess` sees no amendments to discharge and no new items, and carries the partial answer into a complete approval. The unanswered owner decision is silently lost. Require a fully answered source gate and reconcile its outstanding required decisions before allowing a carry; a non-pending P1 row alone is insufficient.

label: Medium
summary: Pending delta checks lose their usable dispatch state after moving or restoring a run. The new `CarryCheck` stores absolute prompt/result paths and command lines (`lib/autoplan-carry.ts:137-153`), but `readState` only relocates the existing plan and phase-attempt paths (`lib/autoplan-state.ts:114-121`); it never relocates `state.carry.check` or its saved lines. A checkpoint restored at a different output directory therefore keeps paths into the old machine's run. Furthermore, `resumeRun` only emits carry instructions when it creates a new gate, not when it resumes an already `gate_pending` check, and `next`/`status` emit ordinary gate instructions instead. After machine replacement, the normal resume flow neither redisplays a usable delta-review dispatch nor marks it execution-unknown, while its reservation remains outstanding. Relocate the carry paths and re-emit the pending check on resume/next/status, with an explicit execution-unknown state when its prior execution cannot be established.
